title: Numeric operators
summary: Integers are exact. Floats are close approximations. Division and remainder have rules that are worth knowing by heart.

sections.heading: Three kinds of division
sections.body:
`/` always gives a float: `7 / 2` is `3.5`.

`//` is floor division and rounds toward negative infinity: `7 // 2` is `3`, but `-7 // 2` is `-4`.

`%` is the remainder that keeps this identity true: `a == (a // b) * b + a % b`. So `-7 % 2` is `1`.

sections.heading: Why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3
sections.body: A Python float is a 64-bit binary number (IEEE 754 double precision). Just as 1/3 has no finite decimal form, 0.1 has no finite binary form, so it is stored as the nearest binary fraction. The tiny errors show up when you add. Compare floats with a tolerance, using `math.isclose(a, b)`, not with `==`.

sections.heading: Integers have no fixed size
sections.body: Unlike in many languages, Python integers grow as large as they need to, so `2 ** 100` is exact and there is no integer overflow.
